# Repository hygiene

Run `pnpm check:repo` from the repository root before committing. The check scans tracked and unignored files for terminal ANSI dumps, known accidental root filenames, credential-shaped content, and files larger than 1 MB. `pnpm test:repo-hygiene` proves the scanner rejects the fake ANSI fixture under `scripts/fixtures/repository-hygiene/`; only that intentional ANSI fixture is excluded from the normal repository scan, so other files added to the directory remain subject to credential and size checks.

## Intentional generated files

| Files | Source and regeneration |
|---|---|
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | pnpm workspace lockfile; regenerate with `pnpm install`. |
| `packages/db/drizzle/*.sql`, `packages/db/drizzle/meta/*.json` | Drizzle schema snapshots and SQL migrations; regenerate a new migration with `pnpm --filter @kobi/db db:generate`. Existing migrations are immutable history. |
| `apps/web/public/auth/*.png` | Deterministic authentication illustrations; regenerate with `pnpm --filter @kobi/web generate:auth-images`. |

`apps/web/public/class_creation_illustration.jpg` is a manually maintained source asset, not generated by a repository script. Worker development generators write activity output to stdout or `/tmp/kobi-artifacts`; generated activity HTML and manifests must not be committed.

## Demo and sample data

Most demo inputs stay in explicitly named development or test paths such as `apps/worker/src/demoTranscript.ts`, `apps/worker/src/dev/`, test files, and `scripts/fixtures/`. The web store still bundles invented `defaultClasses` in `apps/web/src/lib/store.ts` and initializes with that seed, so it remains demo-only data in production web code; until that seed is removed or placed behind an explicit demo/test path, the repository must not claim that all demo data is quarantined to named demo paths. Production flows should read Supabase state and server-side environment variables; do not copy credentials, raw classroom recordings, transcripts, or real student data into documentation or fixtures.
